- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (e.g., drop >0.67 in last 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to news spikes (high news volume) — if news volume >3.0 and sentiment is neutral or bullish, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for volatility.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model often underestimates downside risk — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if recent 5-day average price is >80, model tends to overestimate; cap forecast at 82–83 unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture rebound potential.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00) are common — reduce forecast by 1–2% after 3–5 days of high sentiment to avoid overcorrection.
